first: the drain pipe under the kitchen sink leaks when I empty the sink

tenant.situation: When you drain a full kitchen sink, water drips from the curved white plastic pipe under the sink into the cabinet. When the sink isn't draining it stays dry.

knows.where: kitchen sink cabinet, the curved plastic pipe where it joins the straight pipe
knows.how_bad: a small puddle in the cabinet each time, maybe a cup of water
knows.tried: put a towel and a pan under it
knows.appearance: drips from the joint with a big plastic nut, only while water is draining
knows.dry_otherwise: yes, dry when the tap is off

doesnt_know: whether the nut is loose or the washer is broken

truth.problem: loose slip nut or worn washer on the sink P-trap

judge: Recognises the leak only happens while draining and points to the P-trap joint, suggesting hand-tightening the plastic nut and not using the sink until fixed.
The ticket tells the manager it is a drain-side leak at the trap, not the water supply.

first: 马桶堵了

tenant.situation: Your only toilet won't flush down. The water rises high in the bowl and goes down very slowly. It has not overflowed.

knows.where: the only bathroom, the only toilet in the unit
knows.how_bad: water comes up near the rim and takes about ten minutes to go down
knows.tried: plunged it a few times with a cup plunger, didn't help
knows.what_went_in: normal toilet paper, maybe a lot of it

doesnt_know: whether something is stuck deeper in the pipe

truth.problem: toilet clog in the trapway, other drains fine

judge: Asks whether other drains are fine and whether it is the only toilet, and suggests a flange plunger technique and not flushing again until it drains.
Replies entirely in Chinese and the English ticket notes it is the only toilet.

first: water heatr leaking from the bottom

tenant.situation: There is water on the floor around the bottom of the water heater in the laundry closet. It seems to come from under the tank, not from the pipe on the side.

knows.since: noticed yesterday evening, bigger this morning
knows.how_bad: a puddle about the size of a dinner plate, growing slowly
knows.appearance: water seeping from under the tank, a bit of rust colour
knows.side_pipe: the pipe coming down the side is dry

doesnt_know: the age of the tank
the brand

truth.problem: water heater tank leaking at the base (tank failing)

judge: Checks whether the water comes from the relief valve pipe or the tank itself, and explains how to shut the cold water valve on top if it gets worse.
Tells the manager the tank itself is seeping and the puddle is growing, so it is not mistaken for a relief valve drip.

first: Il n'y a plus d'eau chaude

tenant.situation: No hot water at any tap since this morning. The cold water works fine. The water heater is in a closet; you don't hear it running.

knows.since: this morning, it was fine last night
knows.heater: tall white tank in the closet next to the bathroom, electric (no flame, no gas pipe)
knows.breaker: haven't looked at the electrical panel
knows.tried: ran the tap for five minutes
knows.leaks: no water on the floor around it

doesnt_know: the brand or age of the tank

truth.problem: electric water heater not heating (tripped breaker or failed element)

judge: Asks whether the heater is gas or electric and, being electric, suggests safely checking the breaker labelled for the water heater.
Replies entirely in French.

first: there's a mushroom growing in the corner of my bathroom floor

tenant.situation: A small mushroom is growing where the bathroom floor meets the wall, right next to the tub. The baseboard there feels soft and a bit dark.

knows.where: bathroom, the corner between the end of the tub and the wall
knows.since: saw the mushroom two days ago; the baseboard has looked darker for a few weeks
knows.appearance: one small tan mushroom, the baseboard is soft when pressed, paint bubbling a little
knows.smell: a bit musty in that corner
knows.water: no puddle you can see, the floor is dry on top
knows.tried: pulled the mushroom out, it grew back
knows.tub: you shower in the tub every day

doesnt_know: what is behind the wall
whether a pipe is leaking

truth.problem: slow hidden leak behind the tub wall (tub spout/valve or drain) soaking the subfloor and baseboard

judge: Explains that a mushroom and soft baseboard mean water is getting in from somewhere, likely a slow leak near the tub, rather than treating it as a cleaning problem.
The ticket asks for a leak investigation behind the tub wall, not just mold removal.

first: my hot water smells like rotten eggs

tenant.situation: The hot water smells like rotten eggs at every tap. The cold water smells normal. You don't smell anything in the air near the water heater or the stove.

knows.which_tap: every tap, only the hot side
knows.since: about a week, worse in the morning
knows.gas_smell_in_air: no, the air near the water heater and stove smells normal
knows.heater: tank water heater in the utility closet
knows.tried: ran the hot water for a few minutes, smell fades a bit

doesnt_know: what causes it
whether the heater is gas or electric

truth.problem: sulphur smell from the water heater's anode rod reacting with the water; not a gas leak

judge: Asks once whether the smell is in the air or only in the hot water, then reassures the tenant that a smell only in the hot water usually comes from the water heater, not a gas leak.
Does not keep asking safety questions after the tenant says the air smells normal.

first: toilet keeps running all nite like a waterfall, is that gonna jack up my water bill??

tenant.situation: The toilet tank keeps refilling with a hissing sound, all the time. Every few minutes you hear the water run again.

knows.how_bad: constant hiss, refills every few minutes, flushes fine
knows.bill: you're not sure if water is in your rent

doesnt_know: which part inside the tank is broken

truth.problem: worn flapper or fill valve not shutting off

judge: Answers the bill question honestly without inventing the lease terms (in many BC rentals water is included; the manager can confirm) and explains that a running toilet wastes water so it is worth fixing.
Suggests safe checks like lifting the tank lid to see if the flapper is seated, or turning the toilet's shut-off valve at night.

first: 厕所马桶底下有水

tenant.situation: There is water on the floor around the bottom of the toilet. It shows up after you flush. The tank and the pipe on the wall look dry.

knows.where: the toilet in the main bathroom, around the base where it meets the floor
knows.how_bad: a thin puddle after each flush, you wipe it up
knows.supply_pipe: the little pipe and valve on the wall are dry
knows.tank: the outside of the tank is dry, no drips
knows.wobble: the toilet rocks a little when you sit

doesnt_know: whether the seal under the toilet is broken

truth.problem: failed wax ring seal under a loose toilet

judge: Rules out the tank, supply line and condensation, and connects the leak after flushing and the rocking toilet to the seal at the base.
Replies entirely in Chinese; the ticket notes the toilet rocks, so the manager can plan to reset it.

first: Le robinet de la salle de bain goutte sans arrêt même fermé, je peux vous envoyer une vidéo

tenant.situation: The bathroom sink tap keeps dripping from the spout even when turned off as far as it goes.

knows.which_side: drips whether the lever was last on hot or cold
knows.handle: the lever is a bit stiff
knows.base: dry around the base of the tap

doesnt_know: the brand of the tap

truth.problem: worn cartridge in a single-lever bathroom faucet

judge: Accepts the offered video or photo in the first reply instead of asking questions it would answer.
Tells the tenant not to force the lever and that the manager will replace the worn part; replies entirely in French.

first: water spraying a lil under the kitchen sink from the hose thing, put a bowl under it

tenant.situation: Under the kitchen sink, a thin spray of water is coming from where the flexible hose connects to the little valve on the wall. It sprays all the time, not only when the tap is on.

knows.where: kitchen sink cabinet, left side, the hose going up to the tap
knows.how_bad: a fine spray, the bowl fills in about 20 minutes, cabinet floor wet
knows.when: all the time, even with the tap off
knows.valve: there is a small oval handle on the wall under the sink

doesnt_know: that the valve can shut the water off
whether the hose or the valve is broken

truth.problem: failing braided supply line connection at the shut-off valve

judge: Quickly tells the tenant to turn the small oval shut-off valve clockwise to stop the spray, before asking more questions.
Marks it urgent because it leaks constantly, and the ticket says whether the valve stopped it.

first: hey just fyi the bathroom sink clogged again, I got it going with the plunger but this is like the 3rd time since summer

tenant.situation: The bathroom sink drained very slowly and filled with water. You plunged it and now it drains normally. It has happened about three times since summer.

knows.since: first time in July, then September, now today
knows.tried: plunger each time; once cleaned hair out of the stopper
knows.stopper: pop-up stopper, hair gets caught on it

doesnt_know: whether the pipe in the wall is partly blocked

truth.problem: recurring partial clog in the bathroom sink drain (hair, buildup past the trap)

judge: Acknowledges it is working now and does not walk the tenant through unclogging steps they already did.
Logs a low-urgency ticket that stresses the repeat clogs so the manager can have the drain line cleaned properly.

first: shower drain is so slow im standing in water up to my ankles

tenant.situation: When you shower, water builds up in the tub and takes a long time to go down after you turn the water off.

knows.since: getting slower over a month, bad this week
knows.how_bad: about 3 cm of water while showering, drains in 15 minutes after
knows.other_drains: toilet and sink are fine, no water coming up anywhere else
knows.hair: two people with long hair use it

doesnt_know: how far down the clog is

truth.problem: hair clog in the tub drain

judge: Asks whether other drains are fine, then suggests safe steps like pulling hair from the drain cover and avoiding chemical drain cleaners.
Does not treat it as a sewage backup.

first: theres a brown stain on my bathroom ceiling and now its dripping when the people upstairs shower

tenant.situation: A brown stain on your bathroom ceiling has grown bigger and now drips into your bathroom, mostly in the mornings and evenings when you hear the upstairs neighbours' shower running.

knows.where: bathroom ceiling, above the tub, about a foot from the wall
knows.since: stain noticed two weeks ago, dripping started yesterday
knows.how_bad: a drip every few seconds while they shower, the stain is the size of a pizza, paint bubbling
knows.when: only while the shower upstairs runs
knows.light: the drip is not near the light or the fan
knows.neighbours: haven't talked to the people upstairs

doesnt_know: what is leaking upstairs
the unit number above, maybe 402

truth.problem: leak from the shower in the unit above (failed caulking or shower valve) coming through the ceiling

judge: Asks whether the drip is near any light or electrical fixture, tells the tenant to keep a bucket under it, and does not ask them to fix the neighbour's shower.
The ticket makes clear the source is likely the unit above so the manager arranges access there, and marks it urgent because it is damaging the ceiling.

first: kitchen tap barely has any pressure anymore. also while ur at it the toilet runs sometimes

tenant.situation: The kitchen tap only gives a weak stream on both hot and cold. The bathroom sink and shower are fine. Separately, the toilet sometimes refills by itself for a few seconds.

knows.which_tap: only the kitchen tap is weak, bathroom tap and shower are normal
knows.since: since the building shut the water off for work last week
knows.how_bad: a thin stream, takes ages to fill a pot
knows.tap_end: there's a little screen piece at the end of the spout
knows.toilet: refills for a few seconds every hour or so, flushes fine

doesnt_know: that debris can block the aerator after a shut-off

truth.problem: aerator clogged with debris after the building water shut-off; plus a slow-leaking toilet flapper

judge: Establishes that only the kitchen tap is weak and links it to the recent shut-off, suggesting the tenant unscrew and rinse the aerator.
Does not forget the toilet: both problems end up in the ticket.

first: 家里完全没水了，所有水龙头都没有

tenant.situation: No water comes out of any tap, the shower, or the toilet tank refill. Hot and cold both. It was fine an hour ago.

knows.notice: didn't see any notice in the lobby or elevator
knows.leaks: no water on any floor, no sound of running water

doesnt_know: whether the city or building shut the water off
where the unit's main valve is

truth.problem: water supply to the unit is off (building or city shut-off, or the unit valve closed)

judge: Asks whether it is all taps or one, whether neighbours or a building notice suggest a shut-off, and whether any water is leaking anywhere.
Treats it as urgent (no water, no toilet) and replies entirely in Chinese.

first: kitchen tap no water at all but bathroom is fine?? its like -12 out lol

tenant.situation: Nothing comes out of the kitchen tap, hot or cold. The bathroom taps and toilet work. It is very cold outside.

knows.which_tap: only the kitchen sink, both hot and cold
knows.since: this morning, it worked last night
knows.wall: the sink is on the outside wall under a window, the cabinet feels very cold
knows.leaks: no water in the cabinet, no wet spots on the wall
knows.tried: turned the tap on and off

doesnt_know: whether a pipe is frozen or burst

truth.problem: frozen supply pipe in the exterior wall behind the kitchen sink

judge: Recognises a likely frozen pipe on the outside wall and gives safe steps: open the cabinet doors, warm the room, leave the tap open, and never use a flame or heat gun.
Asks the tenant to watch for any leak as it thaws and to shut off water and report right away if one appears.

first: Ça sent les égouts dans la buanderie depuis quelques jours

tenant.situation: There is a sewer smell in the laundry room, strongest near the round drain in the floor. Nothing is coming up from it.

knows.where: laundry room, near the small round drain in the floor
knows.how_bad: strong when you open the door, fades in the rest of the unit
knows.drain: floor drain, dry, you never pour water in it
knows.backup: no water or dirt coming up, sinks and toilet drain normally
knows.gas: it smells like sewer, not gas

doesnt_know: that a dry drain trap lets sewer gas through

truth.problem: dried-out trap on a rarely used floor drain letting sewer gas in

judge: Confirms nothing is backing up and suggests pouring a few litres of water into the floor drain to refill its trap.
Does not treat it as a gas leak or a sewage backup; replies entirely in French.

first: theres water on the floor in my hallway idk where its coming from

tenant.situation: A wet patch on the hallway floor along the wall that backs onto the bathroom. It comes back every morning after you dry it.

knows.where: hallway, along the wall shared with the bathroom, near the bathroom door
knows.how_bad: a wet strip about 50 cm long, the laminate edge is starting to lift
knows.when: wet again each morning, even when no one showered
knows.other_side: on the bathroom side the toilet is against that wall; the floor around the toilet looks dry

doesnt_know: what is behind the wall
tenant.style: vague at first, more helpful when asked specific things

truth.problem: slow leak at the toilet supply valve inside the shared wall, wicking under the hallway floor

judge: Narrows the source with simple questions (what is on the other side of the wall, the ceiling above, any appliances) instead of guessing.
The ticket points the manager to the shared bathroom wall near the toilet and notes the flooring is lifting.

first: my sink is leaking

tenant.situation: There is water in the cabinet under the kitchen sink. It gets wetter after you wash dishes.

knows.where_water: pooling on the cabinet floor, under the pipes
knows.when: mostly after running the tap or emptying the sink
knows.how_much: a small puddle, a few spoonfuls

doesnt_know: which pipe joint it is

truth.problem: loose slip nut on the kitchen sink drain trap

judge: Asks which sink and whether it leaks only while water drains, the question that tells a drain leak from a supply leak.
Suggests a bowl or towel and not running that sink until it's fixed.

first: toilet overflowing water all over the bathroom floor help

tenant.situation: You flushed and the toilet bowl kept filling and spilled over. Water is on the bathroom floor and starting to reach the hallway carpet.

knows.still_running: yes, water is still coming into the bowl
knows.how_much: about a centimetre on the floor, reaching the hallway
knows.shutoff_valve: there's a little valve on the wall behind the toilet

doesnt_know: what's blocking it

truth.problem: toilet clog with the fill valve still running, overflowing

judge: The first reply tells them to turn the small valve behind the toilet clockwise to stop the water, before any questions.
